MS-ARC01|A component owns a cohesive responsibility behind an explicit boundary.|Orders and invoices have separate owners. Which model clarifies their interaction?|Separate their responsibilities and specify the calls crossing the boundary.|Independent releases are required but a billing invariant crosses both domains. Which design addresses both?|Separate ownership and coordinate the invariant through an explicit versioned contract.

MS-ARC02|Architecture alternatives are evaluated against stated constraints and quality attributes.|A team compares synchronous calls and queued work. What comparison supports its decision?|Compare latency, failure handling and consistency for the actual workload.|A queue absorbs bursts but delays consistency. Which decision process handles that tradeoff?|Measure both alternatives against latency and consistency targets and record the accepted compromise.

MS-ARC03|An integration contract defines exchanged data, semantics, failures and compatibility.|A consumer retries after losing a response. Which contract detail makes retry behavior clear?|Specify request identity, duplicate handling and success and failure meanings.|Consumers upgrade independently. What contract strategy supports gradual evolution?|Use compatible schema changes, explicit version support and consumer verification before retirement.

MS-ARC04|A service quality target defines a measurable outcome under a specified workload.|A requirement says the API must be fast. Which replacement can be verified?|Specify a latency percentile, workload, observation window and threshold.|Caching improves latency but may return stale inventory. What specification makes the compromise reviewable?|Define separate latency and freshness targets and evaluate both under a representative workload.

MS-ARC05|A decision record captures context, alternatives, the decision and its consequences.|A developer asks why a shared database was chosen. Which record answers that question?|Record the constraints, rejected alternatives and consequences of that choice.|A constraint behind an old decision no longer applies. What should happen to the record?|Reassess the alternatives and record a superseding decision while preserving the original rationale.

MS-ARC06|Change-impact analysis traces affected consumers, dependencies and invariants.|An event field changes meaning. What investigation should precede release?|Identify consumers and downstream transformations depending on that meaning.|The change affects APIs, events and reports released at different times. Which plan addresses the impact?|Map affected contracts, stage compatible transitions and verify consumers before removing old behavior.

MS-CORE01|A program implements explicit input, processing and output behavior.|A script reads a record count from a file. How should malformed numeric input be handled?|Validate conversion and produce a defined error before processing records.|A batch may crash halfway and be rerun. Which design avoids repeating committed effects?|Use stable operation identities and recoverable checkpoints with repeat-safe output writes.

MS-CORE02|Version control records related changes and supports review and reconciliation.|Developers changed the same setting for different reasons. How should the conflict be resolved?|Compare both intentions with the current requirement and reconcile the value explicitly.|A release needs one urgent fix from a branch with unfinished work. What limits unrelated changes?|Apply the isolated fix to the release branch and review its dependencies and integration record.

MS-CORE03|A verifiable change connects an observable requirement to explicit acceptance conditions.|A story permits cancelling an order. What makes its acceptance conditions precise?|Specify the authorized actor, allowed order states and observable cancellation result.|Stakeholders disagree about cancellation after dispatch. What prevents an unsupported implementation?|Resolve the conflicting business rule and record the accepted state transitions before implementation.

MS-CORE04|A controlled release uses a known artifact, rollout checks and a recovery plan.|A deployment fails its readiness check. What release action fits that evidence?|Stop promotion and follow the defined recovery path to a compatible artifact.|A release changes code and stored data. What makes recovery planning adequate?|Stage compatible schema changes and identify which application versions can run at each transition.

MS-DE01|A data model represents entities, relationships, keys and relevant constraints.|An order contains several products with quantities. Which model retains those facts?|Use an order-line entity linked to the order and product with quantity on the line.|A reporting model repeats customer attributes for faster reads. What should govern the choice?|Balance query needs against update consistency and define how repeated attributes are refreshed.

MS-DE02|A data processor applies defined transformations to inputs and produces controlled outputs.|Some monetary rows lack required currency codes. What should precede aggregation?|Validate currency requirements and route invalid rows through an explicit exception path.|Large files must be processed with bounded memory and restart support. Which design fits?|Stream bounded batches and commit recoverable checkpoints with repeat-safe outputs.

MS-DE03|A warehouse organizes integrated historical data for analytical queries.|An analyst needs monthly sales by product. Which structure directly supports that query?|Define the sales fact grain and link facts to product and date dimensions.|Customer attributes must be reported as they were when a sale occurred. What preserves that history?|Use effective-dated dimension versions and link each fact to the applicable version.

MS-DE04|A source-to-target mapping defines how source fields become target meanings.|A source price is in cents but its target uses decimal currency. What must the mapping state?|Specify unit conversion, precision and treatment of missing or invalid values.|Two systems assign different meanings to one status code. What prevents semantic corruption?|Define business meanings and explicit conversions, including how unmapped statuses are handled.

MS-DE05|Data quality measures fitness using explicit validity, completeness and consistency rules.|An imported file contains repeated customer identifiers. Which check detects the problem?|Check identifier uniqueness within the required business scope before accepting records.|A strict rejection rule blocks a critical feed during an incident. What preserves quality visibility?|Quarantine affected records, quantify impact and use an explicitly approved recovery path.

MS-DE06|Metadata documents definitions, structure, ownership and usage context.|Several teams use a column called score. What information makes it interpretable?|Record its definition, scale, owner, calculation and expected null behavior.|A field keeps its type but changes meaning. How should metadata handle the change?|Version the definition and preserve its previous meaning for historical interpretation.

MS-DE07|Pipeline monitoring observes freshness, execution status, throughput and quality signals.|A pipeline succeeds but reports show two-day-old data. Which signal reveals the problem?|Compare the latest delivered data timestamp with the freshness target.|One source outage produces thousands of repeated alerts. Which monitoring design improves response?|Correlate related failures and alert on actionable impact while retaining diagnostic events.

MS-DE08|An integration flow defines sources, transformations, destinations and delivery behavior.|Two sources identify the same customer with different keys. What must be defined?|Specify identity matching and the handling of unmatched or conflicting records.|A destination must remain available during upstream outages. Which design states the compromise?|Buffer recoverable changes and define staleness, replay and reconciliation behavior.

MS-DE09|Profiling measures actual distributions, nulls, duplicates and source patterns.|A team assumes postal codes are numeric. What should it profile before choosing a type?|Inspect actual values including leading zeros, letters and missing-value patterns.|A clean small sample hides rare formats that break full loads. Which profiling strategy helps?|Use representative partitions and anomaly summaries, then validate critical assumptions against broader coverage.

MS-DE10|Extraction retrieves a defined source slice with explicit progress boundaries.|A source offers updated_at for incremental extraction. What must a run retain?|A stable watermark and a rule for records sharing or arriving around the boundary.|Late records have nonunique timestamps. Which extraction design reduces omissions?|Use a tie-breaker or overlap window with stable deduplication and a late-arrival policy.

MS-DE11|Transformation rules convert source values into defined target meanings.|Dates arrive in two supported formats. What should a transformation do?|Parse those formats explicitly and route ambiguous or invalid dates for handling.|A new rule changes historical financial totals. What rollout preserves interpretability?|Version the transformation and distinguish recomputed results from the original release.

MS-DE12|Retry-safe orchestration repeats work without duplicating committed effects.|Output rows were inserted before an acknowledgement was lost. What should a retry use?|Use a stable task identity and idempotent or deduplicated output writes.|Dependent tasks partially succeed before a worker crashes. What supports recovery?|Persist task states and dependencies and reconcile committed effects before advancing dependents.

MS-DE13|Warehouse optimization aligns storage and execution with observed analytical workloads.|A report scans date ranges unrelated to its filter. What should be evaluated?|Evaluate date-aware pruning or partitioning using the actual query plan.|An index speeds reporting but slows ingestion substantially. What makes the decision defensible?|Compare total workload costs and retain it only if measured benefit meets operational constraints.

MS-DE14|Secure data handling controls exposure through classification, access and controlled processing.|A test pipeline needs customer-like structure but not real identities. What reduces exposure?|Use representative synthetic or properly de-identified data with the required structural properties.|Analysts need aggregates from sensitive records. Which design balances utility and disclosure risk?|Minimize raw access and evaluate aggregate disclosure risk while validating analytical usefulness.

MS-DE15|Pipeline testing checks transformations, boundaries and resulting data invariants.|Accepted transaction value must be preserved by a transformation. What checks that rule?|Compare the accepted-input total with the transformed-output total.|Unit checks pass but source schema changes break the pipeline. What coverage is missing?|Verify versioned source contracts and representative end-to-end cases including incompatible changes.

MS-DE16|Lineage traces how data depends on upstream sources and transformations.|A source column will be removed. Which lineage information supports impact analysis?|Identify downstream transformations, fields and reports derived from that column.|A dashboard total is wrong after several processing stages. Which capability makes investigation actionable?|Trace the value through versioned transformations and source batches with reproducible provenance.

MS-FS01|Interface design connects user goals to understandable controls and feedback.|Users repeatedly miss the action needed to finish a form. What should be investigated?|Clarify the primary action and required information at the point of decision.|One dense screen serves expert and occasional users. What balances their needs?|Keep frequent actions direct and progressively reveal advanced options, validating both user flows.

MS-FS02|Accessibility provides usable semantics, focus behavior and nonvisual alternatives.|A dialog opens but keyboard focus remains behind it. What should happen?|Move focus inside, contain keyboard navigation and restore focus when the dialog closes.|A custom control looks correct but assistive technology cannot operate it. What should be evaluated?|Its semantics, accessible name, exposed state and keyboard behavior across the intended flow.

MS-FS03|An application interface defines request, response and error contracts.|An API accepts a count that must be positive. Where should the invariant be enforced?|Validate it on the server and return a defined client error for invalid input.|Old clients remain deployed while an endpoint evolves. Which strategy limits compatibility failures?|Use compatible additions or explicit versions and verify consumers before removing the old contract.

MS-FS04|A query selects or modifies data according to a defined model.|A report needs customers with no orders. Which query structure expresses that condition?|Use an anti-join or NOT EXISTS linked to each customer.|Correct queries become slow as tenant data grows. What should guide optimization?|Inspect execution plans, cardinality and tenant predicates under a representative bounded workload.

MS-FS05|Integration connects independent components through agreed behavior.|A payment adapter receives the same success event twice. What should it do?|Correlate event identity and apply the business effect idempotently.|Components cannot share one database transaction. Which design supports recoverable delivery?|Commit local state with a durable event and make downstream processing idempotent and reconcilable.

MS-FS06|Debugging narrows reproducible faults through observations and testable hypotheses.|A failure occurs for one input shape. What should be captured first?|Capture a minimal failing input and the expected versus observed behavior.|A timing fault disappears under verbose logging. Which investigation reduces misleading conclusions?|Use low-impact correlated observations and test competing timing hypotheses under controlled conditions.

MS-FS07|Unit tests check focused observable behavior against explicit expectations.|A function must reject empty input. Which assertion directly checks the behavior?|Call it with empty input and assert the specified rejection result.|Tests mirror private methods and break during harmless restructuring. How should they improve?|Check stable observable contracts and retain cases that detect meaningful behavioral regressions.

MS-FS08|Code review examines a change for correctness, maintainability and relevant risks.|A change trusts the organization ID sent by a browser. What should the reviewer question?|Verify trusted server tenant context and tenant enforcement in storage operations.|A security fix is mixed with extensive unrelated refactoring. Which review strategy improves confidence?|Isolate concerns and review the security-relevant data flow with focused evidence.

MS-FS09|Responsive layout adapts content to available space while preserving usability.|A narrow screen clips a form's submit action. What should change?|Reflow content and keep the action reachable without clipping.|A phone view must retain critical identifiers in a wide table. Which approach fits?|Preserve essential information with deliberate horizontal access or an equivalent compact representation.

MS-FS10|Semantic HTML expresses element meaning and built-in interaction behavior.|A clickable div performs a form action. Which element normally fits?|A button with an appropriate accessible name and button type.|A complex table cannot rely only on visual positions. What should its structure retain?|Meaningful table headers and explicitly labelled controls that expose relationships nonvisually.

MS-FS11|Asynchronous requests finish independently of the initiating interaction.|The first search response arrives after a newer one. What should the UI do?|Apply only the response for the current query or cancel obsolete requests.|A save times out after the server may have committed. What retry behavior avoids duplicates?|Reuse a stable operation key and recover the server outcome before issuing a distinct mutation.

MS-FS12|Validation checks structure and business constraints at a trusted boundary.|A client removes the minimum constraint from a quantity field. What must the API do?|Reject quantities violating the server-validated business rule.|Two valid individual fields violate a combined invariant. Where should it be checked?|Validate their combination in the owning use case and enforce critical storage constraints.

MS-FS13|Authorization determines whether an identity may act on a specific resource.|A valid user changes an invoice ID to another tenant's invoice. What must be checked?|Verify tenant scope and permission for that exact resource.|Roles change during a long workflow. What protects its later mutations?|Recheck current trusted membership and resource scope at consequential operations.

MS-FS14|Transactions group changes under defined consistency and failure behavior.|An order and stock reservation must commit together. What should coordinate them?|Use one suitable transaction when both share the database boundary.|Two requests compete for the last stock unit. What protects the invariant?|Use a conditional update or lock and verify the affected-row result before confirming success.

MS-FS15|Refactoring changes internal structure while preserving intended observable behavior.|Two functions duplicate a validated calculation. What is a safe restructuring goal?|Extract shared behavior behind a stable interface while preserving its observable contract.|A legacy module has unclear behavior and many callers. What reduces restructuring risk?|Characterize critical contracts and compare observable results while changing small boundaries.

MS-FS16|Continuous integration checks combined changes using a reproducible pipeline.|A build works only on one developer machine. Which property should be established?|Declared dependencies and repeatable build steps in a controlled clean environment.|A fast pipeline omits checks for changed integration contracts. How should it be evaluated?|Balance feedback time against risk and retain required checks for affected boundaries.

MS-GOV01|Data ownership assigns accountability for definitions, quality and permitted use.|Teams disagree about authority to approve a data definition. What resolves responsibility?|An explicit owner and steward assignment for the dataset and decision type.|One producer serves many consuming teams. Which ownership model avoids ambiguity?|Name an accountable owner and explicit producer, steward and consumer responsibilities with escalation.

MS-GOV02|Governance rules define approved responsibilities, controls and decision procedures.|A team needs to know who can grant dataset access. What should its rule state?|Decision authority, approval criteria and the evidence that must be retained.|Teams interpret a policy differently. What makes it operational?|Define its scope, decision criteria, responsibilities and verifiable control steps.

MS-GOV03|Lifecycle compliance checks collection, use, retention and disposal against applicable documented rules.|A dataset reaches its retention deadline. What should precede disposal?|Check the applicable retention decision and any documented hold or authorized exception.|Backups retain records scheduled for active-system deletion. What assessment is necessary?|Document retention and recovery-copy handling under the applicable rules and authorized exceptions.

MS-INF01|Connectivity verification examines addressing, routing, name resolution and reachability.|An endpoint works by IP but not by hostname. What is the direct check?|Inspect name resolution and the hostname's configured address records.|A network change affects several dependent services. Which verification is adequate?|Verify required paths, resolution and protocols from the actual deployment locations before promotion.

MS-INF02|Provisioning creates resources from explicit infrastructure requirements and configuration.|Two environments should be identical except for size. What reduces hidden differences?|Repeatable declared resource definitions with explicit environment parameters.|An update may replace a stateful volume. What must precede application?|Inspect the change plan and establish a validated preservation or migration path for its data.

MS-INF03|Automation encodes repeatable infrastructure operations with explicit inputs and outcomes.|A scheduler may rerun one provisioning task. What should its changes do?|Converge to the intended state without duplicating already satisfied resources.|An operation fails after changing only some hosts. What supports safe recovery?|Use observable checkpoints, bounded changes and reconciliation for partially applied state.

MS-INF04|Configuration records capture intended settings, ownership and change history.|Servers have differing undocumented timeouts. What should be recorded?|The intended value, affected resources, rationale and responsible owner.|An emergency setting differs from the declared baseline. What follow-up preserves accuracy?|Record the exception and explicitly reconcile the baseline or restore the approved setting.

MS-INF05|Health monitoring distinguishes process activity from readiness to deliver required service.|A process runs but cannot reach its essential database. What reflects readiness?|A check of the dependency needed for essential request handling.|Dependency failures cause restart loops that worsen recovery. What design should be evaluated?|Separate liveness from readiness and do not equate every transient dependency fault with process failure.

MS-INF06|Fault investigation correlates symptoms, changes and dependencies to narrow causes.|Several applications fail after a routing change. Which evidence should be correlated first?|Failure timing and affected paths against that exact change and dependency reachability.|Restarting temporarily hides an intermittent fault. What preserves useful evidence?|Capture correlated system observations before disruptive actions and test the cause against the incident timeline.

MS-INF07|Backup usefulness depends on restoring and verifying the required data.|A backup job succeeded. What demonstrates recoverability?|An authorized restore exercise that verifies recovered data and application behavior.|The business defines recovery-time and recovery-point targets. What should guide the strategy?|Measure restoration duration and data-loss characteristics against both targets using a representative procedure.

MS-INF08|Hardening and updates reduce exposure while preserving required functionality.|An update changes a security-sensitive configuration. What should be verified afterward?|The intended security setting and required application behavior.|A critical update may be incompatible with a stateful service. Which rollout balances concerns?|Assess exposure and compatibility, validate a staged update and retain a compatible recovery path.

MS-QA01|A test plan relates risks, scope, prerequisites and acceptance evidence.|A release changes monetary calculations. What should identify its important checks?|Map calculation risks to acceptance conditions and representative scenarios.|Time is limited across several critical workflows. Which planning choice is defensible?|Prioritize by impact and likelihood and disclose omitted coverage while retaining required evidence.

MS-QA02|A test suite organizes cases, expectations and reusable setup for a purpose.|Cases require an account to be active. What should setup define?|Define and verify the account prerequisite instead of depending on another case's execution.|Many cases fail because of one shared setup fault. What improves diagnosis?|Separate setup failures from behavior failures and make case prerequisites and isolation explicit.

MS-QA03|Test execution compares observations with expectations in a known environment.|A required service is unavailable. How should the case be recorded?|As blocked or not executed with the concrete dependency, not passed.|A rerun passes after an initial failure. What record preserves evidence?|Retain both runs and changed conditions without counting the rerun as independent coverage.

MS-QA04|A defect report gives context, reproduction, expected behavior and observed evidence.|A report only says the page is broken. What makes it actionable?|Relevant environment, reproducible steps and expected versus actual results.|Several symptoms might share one cause. How should findings be documented?|Keep traceable observations, separate facts from hypotheses and link related reports without inventing a cause.

MS-QA05|Reproduction establishes the conditions under which an observed issue occurs.|A customer issue depends on locale and input format. What should be captured?|The locale, exact input shape and relevant application version.|Sensitive production data cannot be reused for reproduction. Which approach supports investigation?|Create representative non-sensitive conditions and document behaviorally relevant differences from production.

MS-QA06|Automated tests encode repeatable checks of observable behavior and expectations.|A browser check selects a control by changing pixel position. What is a better dependency?|A stable semantic locator tied to the intended control or behavior.|A check verifies only that Save was clicked. What stronger evidence is needed?|Verify resulting state through the appropriate contract and distinguish requests from committed outcomes.

MS-QA07|Integration tests examine collaborating components across real boundaries.|A query passes with a fake adapter but fails against the database. What coverage is missing?|A focused check using the real database contract and representative schema.|Producer and consumer contracts evolve independently. Which strategy reveals incompatibility earlier?|Verify versioned expectations and exercise the relevant combined integration flows.

MS-QA08|Exploration follows a focused charter while adapting investigation to observations.|A tester explores failures during form retries. What charter provides focus?|Investigate interrupted submissions, duplicate actions and recovery feedback with recorded state observations.|Exploration finds a possible issue outside its charter. What is appropriate?|Record evidence and the hypothesis, then pursue or hand off an explicitly bounded follow-up.

MS-QA09|Equivalence partitioning groups inputs expected to share relevant behavior.|A quantity accepts integers from 1 to 50. Which partitions are useful?|In-range integers, below-range values, above-range values and non-integer inputs.|Several business categories interact in one input. What makes partitioning adequate?|Define meaningful behavior categories and inspect combinations that challenge assumptions between them.

MS-QA10|Boundary analysis selects values around points where behavior changes.|A field permits 1 through 50 inclusively. Which values target its boundaries?|Values just below, at and just above each endpoint.|Several ordered limits constrain one request. What checks their interaction?|Exercise each transition and combinations crossing another field's dependent limit.

MS-QA11|Risk-based testing prioritizes evidence by failure likelihood and impact.|A rare fault exposes another tenant's records. What should influence its priority?|Consider the severe impact alongside the likelihood.|A critical low-frequency path lacks evidence while a cosmetic path is well covered. What allocation is defensible?|Address the significant evidence gap and document the remaining risk explicitly.

MS-QA12|Test preparation establishes controlled data, services and configuration prerequisites.|A case needs one active membership. What should setup verify?|The exact membership and relevant environment before interpreting behavior.|Shared data changes during concurrent checks. What improves reliability?|Use isolated or coordinated state and record fixture versions and relevant conditions.

MS-QA13|Defect impact describes consequences for users and business operations.|A fault prevents all order submissions. Which impact factor matters most?|Loss of a core capability across the affected user population.|Similar visual symptoms cause different data consequences. How should impact be compared?|Assess scope, integrity, recoverability and business consequences rather than appearance alone.

MS-QA14|Regression checks establish whether existing required behavior survives a change.|A shared validation helper changes. What guides case selection?|Its consumers and previously required behaviors affected by the contract change.|A release has a large suite but limited time. Which strategy is defensible?|Combine impact-based selection with required safeguards and disclose coverage not exercised.

MS-QA15|Performance evaluation measures behavior under a defined workload and environment.|A latency number has no workload or sample description. What is needed?|The workload, sample scope, environment and measurement definition.|Median latency passes but bursts violate a tail target. What addresses the requirement?|Measure the required percentile and errors under representative bursts while correlating resource constraints.

MS-QA16|A flaky check changes outcome without a relevant intended behavior change.|A case intermittently fails while awaiting asynchronous updates. What should be investigated?|Observable completion, timing assumptions and shared-state interference.|Long sleeps hide failures but slow the suite. What targets the cause?|Use explicit bounded completion signals and investigate nondeterministic dependencies instead of arbitrary delays.

MS-SEC01|Security risk relates a threat scenario, exposed assets, likelihood and impact.|An endpoint may expose confidential records. What should precede control selection?|Identify affected assets, the plausible threat path and consequences.|Several risks compete for limited effort. What supports prioritization?|Use documented likelihood, impact and control effectiveness with accountable acceptance of residual risk.

MS-SEC02|A control addresses a defined security risk and must be verified for its effect.|An access restriction was configured. What evidence checks its protection?|Verify permitted and denied resource operations under representative trusted identities.|A control reduces one threat but adds failure modes. What evaluation is needed?|Compare risk reduction, bypass opportunities and operational consequences in the intended context.

MS-SEC03|Identity and access controls link authenticated identities to limited authorized actions.|A departed employee still has a session. What behavior should be checked?|Enforce revoked membership or rights on subsequent protected operations.|A service account needs only one processing task. What access design reduces unnecessary authority?|Use a dedicated identity with narrowly scoped permissions and an explicit credential and access lifecycle.

MS-SEC04|Alert investigation correlates context and evidence to assess suspected security activity.|An unusual-login alert appears. What should precede a compromise conclusion?|Correlate identity, source, timing and related behavior with the expected context.|Many alerts occur during a suspected incident. Which approach avoids unsupported conclusions?|Build a correlated timeline and distinguish confirmed activity from unresolved hypotheses while preserving evidence.

MS-SEC05|Incident response coordinates identification, containment, recovery and accountable communication.|An account may be compromised. Which action should follow the response procedure?|Preserve evidence and use the authorized containment and escalation path.|Containment may interrupt a critical service while evidence is incomplete. What decision process fits?|Assess threat and service impact under accountable incident authority and retain the rationale and evidence.

MS-SEC06|Vulnerability assessment evaluates weaknesses in an explicit authorized scope.|A scanner reports a vulnerable package. What should be verified before prioritizing remediation?|The deployed affected component, applicable conditions and actual exposure.|A severe finding concerns an unreachable feature. What assessment is needed?|Validate reachability and compensating controls while retaining the finding and documented risk decision.

MS-SEC07|Remediation verification checks the actual resolution of an intended weakness.|A team says a package was updated. What should verification establish?|The deployed artifact and the relevant weakness under applicable conditions.|A fix changes authorization elsewhere. What verification addresses both concerns?|Recheck the original weakness and affected security boundaries and retain unresolved side-effect evidence.

MS-SEC08|Control assurance retains traceable evidence that a control meets its objective.|An audit asks whether access reviews occurred. What evidence supports the claim?|Dated scope-specific review records and accountable decisions for the relevant access population.|A control report omits exceptions. How should its evidence improve?|Retain control scope, performed checks, exceptions and their disposition for independent assessment.

MS-SEC09|A security recommendation links a concrete risk to an actionable change and rationale.|A report says improve security without naming a risk. What should be added?|The affected asset, risk, proposed action and verification evidence.|A recommendation has high operational cost and uncertain benefit. How should it be communicated?|Explain assumptions, expected risk reduction, alternatives and residual uncertainty to the accountable owner.

MS-SEC10|A security procedure turns policy intent into repeatable responsibilities and steps.|A policy requires revoking departed staff access. What should its procedure specify?|Triggers, responsible roles, affected systems and evidence of completed revocation.|A procedure no longer matches the identity platform. What maintenance is appropriate?|Review policy intent, update and validate operational steps and preserve versioned responsibility and change records.
